snapshot.stmt: Determine \(m^*(n,B,s,\delta,\sigma,\eta)\) up to universal constants in every regime, and construct a polynomial-real-arithmetic-time exact-budget design-decoder pair whose simultaneous edge and nonedge certificates attain that value. In particular, decide whether the factor \(s+1\) multiplying the noise-to-signal term in the simultaneous-certificate theorem is intrinsic to polynomial-time uniform certification or can be removed while preserving the exact-budget constraint.

defs.def:minimax-pool-complexity: \(m^*=\inf\{m:\exists\ d=((\pi_t)_{t=1}^m,g)\text{ that is an admissible adaptive exact-budget design and decoder, with }\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_s}\Pr_{P,d}(g(\mathscr H_m)\ne A)\le\eta\}\).
defs.def:sharp-frontier-handle: Optimize a constant-row-weight bipartite incidence design for the weakest structured sparse singular direction, decode all outcome rows with a certificate-producing convex program, and dualize the same excitation program into a signed support packing for the minimax converse.

snapshot.stmt:
There are universal constants \(c_0,C_0>0\) with the following property.  Let \(Z\sim\Pi_{m,B}\).  If
\[
 m\ge C_0q^{-1}\left\{(2s+1)\log\!\left(\frac{en}{2s+1}\right)+\log\!\left(\frac2\rho\right)\right\},
\]
then, with probability at least \(1-\rho\), all three conclusions below hold:
\[
 \frac{\lVert Xv\rVert_2^2}{m}\ge c_0q\lVert v\rVert_2^2
 \quad\text{whenever}\quad
 \lVert v\rVert_0\le2s+1,
\]
\[
 \frac{\lVert Xv\rVert_2^2}{m}\ge c_0q\lVert v\rVert_2^2
 \quad\text{whenever there is }S\subseteq\mathcal U, |S|\le s+1,
 \text{ with }\lVert v_{S^c}\rVert_1\le\lVert v_S\rVert_1,
\]
and
\[
 \max_{j\in\mathcal U}\lVert Xe_j\rVert_2^2\le2mq.
\]
If \(n\ge9\), the second conclusion also holds, after decreasing \(c_0\) universally, under the larger cone condition \(\lVert v_{S^c}\rVert_1\le3\lVert v_S\rVert_1\).

defs.def:centered-design: Given \(Z\in\{0,1\}^{m\times n}\) with \(Z_{t\cdot}\in\mathcal Z_B\), set \(H_m=I_m-m^{-1}\mathbf 1_m\mathbf 1_m^{\mathsf T}\) and \(X=H_mZ\).
defs.def:random-balanced-pools: Under \(\Pi_{m,B}\), the rows \(Z_{t\cdot}\) are independent and uniform on \(\mathcal Z_B\); drawing a row is implemented by a uniformly random permutation of \(\mathcal U\) and treating its first \(B\) entries.

snapshot.stmt: Assume in addition that \(n\ge9\). There exist universal constants \(c,C>0\) such that, for \(Z\sim\Pi_{m,B}\), if \(m\ge Cq^{-1}\{(2s+1)\log(en/(2s+1))+\log(2/\rho)\}\), then \(\Pr\{\kappa_s(Z)^2\ge cq,\ \phi_s(Z)^2\ge cq\}\ge1-\rho\). The assignment matrix itself is generated in randomized time polynomial in \(n\) and \(m\).

defs.def:cone-curvature: \(\phi_s(Z)=\min_{i\in\mathcal U}\min_{S\subseteq\mathcal U:\,i\in S,\,|S|\le s+1}\inf\{\lVert Xv\rVert_2/(\sqrt m\lVert v\rVert_2):v\ne0,\ \lVert v_{S^c}\rVert_1\le3\lVert v_S\rVert_1\}\).
defs.def:random-balanced-pools: Under \(\Pi_{m,B}\), the rows \(Z_{t\cdot}\) are independent and uniform on \(\mathcal Z_B\); drawing a row is implemented by a uniformly random permutation of \(\mathcal U\) and treating its first \(B\) entries.

snapshot.stmt: There are universal choices of \(C_{\mathrm{cert}}\) and \(C>0\) such that, if \(Z\sim\Pi_{m,B}\), \(m\ge Cq^{-1}\{(2s+1)\log(en/(2s+1))+(\sigma^2/\delta^2)(s+1)\log(2n^2/\eta)+\log(2/\rho)\}\), and \(P\in\mathcal M_s\), then the displayed sample-size condition implies \(r_m<\delta/2\). Run the real-arithmetic decoder with \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{comp}}=(\delta-2r_m)/8\) and \(R_m=r_m+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{comp}}\). Its primal--dual gap bound and strong convexity give \(\lVert\widehat\theta_i-\theta_i^{\mathrm D}\rVert_2\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{comp}}\), hence the same coordinatewise bound; every row output is computable using a number of real-arithmetic operations polynomial in \(m\), \(n\), and \(\log(1/\varepsilon_{\mathrm{comp}})\). With probability at least \(1-\rho-\eta\), simultaneously for every \(i\in\mathcal U\), \(\lVert\theta_i^{\mathrm D}-\theta_i\rVert_\infty\le r_m\) and therefore \(\lVert\widehat\theta_i-\theta_i\rVert_\infty\le R_m\). The numerical margin is \(\delta-2R_m=3(\delta-2r_m)/4>0\), so simultaneously for all \(i\ne j\), \(C_{ij}=\mathsf{edge}\) if \(A_{ij}=1\) and \(C_{ij}=\mathsf{nonedge}\) if \(A_{ij}=0\). Thus \(\widehat A=A\), no certificate is undecided, and polynomial-precision optimization preserves every inclusion and exclusion certificate. The network-wide probability uses the scalar predictable-design innovation condition for each fixed outcome row at error level \(\eta/n\), followed by a union bound over \(i\in\mathcal U\); no restriction on contemporaneous dependence across outcome rows is imposed.

defs.def:dantzig-decoder: For each \(i\in\mathcal U\), compute \(v_i=\min_{u\in\mathcal D_i}\lVert u\rVert_1\) by linear programming, and define \(\theta_i^{\mathrm D}=\arg\min\{\lVert u\rVert_2^2/2:u\in\mathcal D_i,\ \lVert u\rVert_1\le v_i\}\), which is unique. In the Blum--Shub--Smale real-arithmetic model with oracle access to the observed real coordinates, return a feasible \(\widehat\theta_i\) when the primal--dual gap for this strongly convex quadratic program is at most \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{comp}}^2/2\). When \(r_m<\delta/2\), use the explicit coordinate tolerance \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{comp}}=(\delta-2r_m)/8\).
defs.def:sparse-additive-class: \(\mathcal M_s(n,m,B,\delta,\sigma)=\{P:P\text{ satisfies heterogeneous additive network effects, directed row sparsity, beta-min separation, and the rowwise scalar predictable-design conditionally sub-Gaussian martingale-innovation condition for the displayed indices }n,m,B\}\).
defs.def:support-certificates: For \(i\ne j\), first set \(C_{ij}=\mathsf{edge}\) if \(\lvert(\widehat\theta_i)_j\rvert>R_m\); otherwise set \(C_{ij}=\mathsf{nonedge}\) if \(\lvert(\widehat\theta_i)_j\rvert<\delta-R_m\), and set \(C_{ij}=\mathsf{undecided}\) in the remaining case. Set \(C_{ii}=\mathsf{nonedge}\).

assumptions.ass:additive-interference: For every \(i\in\mathcal U\) and \(z\in\mathcal Z_B\), \(\mu_i(z)=\alpha_i+z^{\mathsf T}\theta_i\).
assumptions.ass:noise-subgaussian: For each fixed \(i\in\mathcal U\), every admissible \(d\), every \(t\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\), and every real \(\lambda\), \(\mathbb E_{P,d}[\exp\{\lambda\varepsilon_{t,i}\}\mid\mathcal F_{t-1},Z_{t\cdot}]\le\exp(\lambda^2\sigma^2/2)\).

snapshot.stmt: There exists a universal constant \(c>0\) such that, on the Gaussian-noise subclass of \(\mathcal M_s\), every admissible adaptive exact-budget design and decoder \(d=((\pi_t)_{t=1}^m,g)\) satisfying \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_s}\Pr_{P,d}(g(\mathscr H_m)\ne A)\le\eta\) obeys \(m\ge c\,\sigma^2(\log(n-1)+\log(1/\eta))/(q\delta^2)\). In the noiseless degree-one subclass, every admissible \(d\) that identifies \(A\) uniformly also obeys \(m\ge\max\{\lceil\log_2(n+2)\rceil,\lceil1/q\rceil\}\).

defs.def:admissible-adaptive-design: \(d=((\pi_t)_{t=1}^m,g)\), where each \(\pi_t(\cdot\mid\mathcal F_{t-1})\) is a predictable probability kernel supported on \(\mathcal Z_B\), and \(g\) is \(\mathcal F_m\)-measurable with values in \(\{0,1\}^{n\times n}\); the terminal estimate is \(\widehat A=g(\mathscr H_m)\).
defs.def:induced-experimental-law: For an environment \(P\) and an admissible \(d\), \(\Pr_{P,d}\) is the unique sequential law satisfying \(Z_{t\cdot}\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}\sim\pi_t(\cdot\mid\mathcal F_{t-1})\) and \(Y_{t\cdot}\mid\mathcal F_{t-1},Z_{t\cdot}\sim K_{P,t}(\cdot\mid\mathcal F_{t-1},Z_{t\cdot})\) for every \(t\); it is undefined unless the complete pair \(d=((\pi_t)_{t=1}^m,g)\) is specified.
defs.def:minimax-pool-complexity: \(m^*=\inf\{m:\exists\ d=((\pi_t)_{t=1}^m,g)\text{ that is an admissible adaptive exact-budget design and decoder, with }\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_s}\Pr_{P,d}(g(\mathscr H_m)\ne A)\le\eta\}\).

assumptions.ass:noise-subgaussian: For each fixed \(i\in\mathcal U\), every admissible \(d\), every \(t\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\), and every real \(\lambda\), \(\mathbb E_{P,d}[\exp\{\lambda\varepsilon_{t,i}\}\mid\mathcal F_{t-1},Z_{t\cdot}]\le\exp(\lambda^2\sigma^2/2)\).

snapshot.stmt:
There is a universal constant \(C>0\) such that, if
\[
 m\ge Cq^{-1}\left\{(s+1)\log\!\left(\frac{8n^3}{\eta}\right)
 +\frac{\sigma^2}{\delta^2}\log\!\left(\frac{8n^2}{\eta}\right)\right\},
\]
then independent uniform exact-budget pools together with the rowwise partially penalized Lasso, leaving coordinate \(i\) unpenalized and using a sufficiently small universal penalty \(c_{\mathrm L}q\delta\), define an admissible exact decoder satisfying
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M_s}\Pr_{P,d}(\widehat A\ne A)\le\eta.
\]
The decoder uses the minimum-Euclidean-norm minimizer off the unique-solution event and declares \(A_{ij}=1\) exactly when the penalized coordinate \(j\ne i\) of the selected minimizer is nonzero.  This is a statistical exact-minimizer statement and makes no finite-precision operation or bit-complexity claim.

snapshot.stmt:
Define
\[
 U_{\mathrm D}=Cq^{-1}\left\{(2s+1)\log\!\left(\frac{en}{2s+1}\right)
 +\frac{\sigma^2}{\delta^2}(s+1)\log\!\left(\frac{4n^2}{\eta}\right)
 +\log\!\left(\frac4\eta\right)\right\}
\]
and
\[
 U_{\mathrm L}=Cq^{-1}\left\{(s+1)\log\!\left(\frac{8n^3}{\eta}\right)
 +\frac{\sigma^2}{\delta^2}\log\!\left(\frac{8n^2}{\eta}\right)\right\},
\]
where \(C>0\) is universal.  Then the presently proved nonasymptotic answer to the sharp-pool-complexity question is the two-sided bracket
\[
 c\,\frac{\sigma^2\{\log(n-1)+\log(1/\eta)\}}{q\delta^2}
 \le m^*(n,B,s,\delta,\sigma,\eta)
 \le \left\lceil\min\{U_{\mathrm D},U_{\mathrm L}\}\right\rceil.
\]
The \(U_{\mathrm D}\) witness is the simultaneous Dantzig certificate with a mathematically valid finite-tolerance optimization certificate; the \(U_{\mathrm L}\) witness is exact rowwise partially penalized Lasso.  Thus the factor \(s+1\) in the Dantzig noise-to-signal term is not intrinsic to exact convex support recovery, but the proved Lasso alternative pays \((s+1)\log(8n^3/\eta)\) for simultaneous empirical strict dual feasibility.  No dimension-only finite-precision complexity guarantee is proved for either optimization output.  Separately, probability-one identification on the noiseless degree-one subclass requires
\[
 m\ge\max\{\lceil\log_2(n+2)\rceil,\lceil1/q\rceil\},
\]
and every fixed design with \(\kappa_s(Z)>0\) requires \(m\ge2s+2\).  The gap between the displayed lower bound and the better of the two upper bounds remains unresolved outside regimes in which their orders coincide.

snapshot.stmt: Starting from the proved two-sided bracket, determine \(m^*(n,B,s,\delta,\sigma,\eta)\) up to universal constants in every regime by either proving an adaptive recovery lower bound that matches the sparse-exploration term or constructing a sharper recovery-valid exact-budget design. Construct a certified polynomial-time finite-precision exact-budget decoder attaining the resulting order, with simultaneous edge and nonedge certificates, and decide which sparsity costs in the two current upper bounds are intrinsic.
